name: AgroSense Agronomic Pathology Offline Knowledge Base
description: Pre-cached diagnostic and treatment guidance for disconnected farm field operations.

early_blight.name: Early Blight
symptoms: Small brown to black spots with characteristic concentric rings creating a target-board pattern.
Yellow chlorotic halos surrounding lesions, primarily beginning on older bottom leaves.
Progressive premature defoliation exposing fruit to sunscald.
Dark, sunken collar rot lesions on lower stems.

bioFungicides: Bacillus subtilis (Serenade ASO) applied at 3.0 - 5.0 ml/L at first sign of spotting.
Copper Octanoate (Copper soap shield) at 2.0 - 3.5 ml/L every 7-10 days.
Trichoderma harzianum soil drench and foliar formulation to suppress fungal sporulation.
botanicalOils: Cold-pressed Neem Oil (0.5% - 1.0% solution, ~5ml/L) with mild horticultural soap emulsifier.
Potassium Bicarbonate foliar spray (3g/L) to alter leaf surface pH against spores.
culturalPractices: Prune lower leaves 12-18 inches from soil surface to prevent soil splash inoculation.
Apply 2-3 inches of organic straw or plastic mulch to barrier spores in soil.
Convert to drip irrigation to keep canopy foliage dry; avoid overhead watering.

chemicalControl.sprayInterval: Apply preventative sprays every 7 to 10 days during warm, humid conditions (75-85°F).
chemicalControl.resistanceManagement: Alternate FRAC Group M5 (Chlorothalonil) with FRAC Group 11 (Azoxystrobin).

late_blight.name: Late Blight
symptoms: Water-soaked, irregular pale green lesions expanding rapidly into dark, greasy brown-black patches.
White cottony sporulation visible on leaf undersides in humid conditions.
Rapid collapse and blackening of whole stems, petioles, and foliage within days.
Firm, dark brown sunken rot on tubers or green/ripe fruit surfaces.

bioFungicides: Copper Hydroxide / Bordeaux Mixture (1% copper sulfate + hydrated lime) applied preventatively.
Bacillus amyloliquefaciens (Double Nickel) applied at 2.5 - 4.0 g/L.
Fixed copper compounds applied every 5-7 days when weather is cool and damp.
botanicalOils: Pure cold-pressed neem extract (10 ml/L) as a protective spore germination inhibitor.
culturalPractices: Immediately rogue and bag completely infected plants; do not leave cull piles near fields.
Maintain wide row spacing (>36 inches) for rapid morning drying.
Eliminate volunteer tomato and potato plants which act as pathogen overwintering reservoirs.

chemicalControl.sprayInterval: High disease pressure requires 5 to 7-day spray intervals. Treat before rain events.
chemicalControl.resistanceManagement: Rotate FRAC Group 40 (Dimethomorph) with FRAC Group 43 (Fluopicolide) and Group 27 (Cymoxanil).

powdery_mildew.name: Powdery Mildew
symptoms: Distinct white to talcum powder-like circular fungal spots on upper and lower leaf surfaces.
Leaves curl upward, turn yellow, desiccate, and turn brown/brittle.
Infected young leaves become distorted and stunted in growth.

bioFungicides: Potassium Bicarbonate (MilStop / Armicarb) at 3.0 - 4.5 g/L for rapid eradicant action.
Bacillus subtilis (Serenade MAX) at 3.0 g/L as a preventative biofilm.
Sulfur dust or wettable sulfur (2.0 - 3.0 g/L) below 85°F.
botanicalOils: Neem oil 0.75% solution (7.5 ml/L water) sprayed thoroughly covering leaf undersides.
Dilute milk spray (40% whole milk, 60% water) exposed to direct sunlight.
culturalPractices: Plant in full sun (>6-8 hours direct sunlight) since UV light inhibits spore germination.
Prune dense canopy foliage to enhance internal airflow.

chemicalControl.sprayInterval: Apply every 7-14 days at first appearance of white powdery colonies.
chemicalControl.resistanceManagement: Alternate DMI fungicides (FRAC 3) with QoI fungicides (FRAC 11).

apple_scab.name: Apple Scab
symptoms: Olive-green to velvety dark brown lesions on leaves with feathery margins.
Velvety brown lesions on fruit developing into corky, cracked scabby patches.

bioFungicides: Liquid Lime Sulfur applied during delayed dormant to pink bud stage.
Wettable sulfur (3.0 - 4.0 g/L) applied before forecast rain events.
culturalPractices: Rake and shred fallen apple leaves in autumn to accelerate leaf decomposition.
Prune trees during dormancy into an open vase or central leader.

chemicalControl.sprayInterval: Green tip through 2nd cover spray every 5-7 days pre-bloom.
chemicalControl.resistanceManagement: Tank-mix systemic fungicides with a protectant (Captan).

bacterial_spot.name: Bacterial Spot
symptoms: Small (1-3mm) dark brown to black angular water-soaked spots on leaves and stems.
Greasy appearance on leaf undersides with narrow yellow halos.
Fruit exhibits raised, scab-like, brown warty blemishes.

bioFungicides: Fixed Copper Hydroxide + Bacillus subtilis tank mix.
culturalPractices: Avoid working in wet fields; use drip irrigation exclusively.
Treat seed with hot water (122°F for 25 minutes for tomato; 125°F for 30 minutes for pepper).
Rotate with non-host crops for at least 2 consecutive seasons.

chemicalControl.sprayInterval: Spray every 5 to 7 days during warm, rainy weather.
chemicalControl.resistanceManagement: Tank-mix copper with mancozeb to overcome copper-tolerant Xanthomonas.

healthy.name: Healthy Plant Baseline
symptoms: Uniform chlorophyll pigmentation, normal turgidity, vigorous growth.
No lesions, yellow halos, wilting, or fungal sporulation.

bioFungicides: Preventative foliar Seaweed extract or Fish Hydrolysate for immune vigor.
culturalPractices: Maintain balanced organic soil nutrition based on periodic soil testing.
Consistent drip irrigation scheduling aligned with evapotranspiration rates.
